So the existing shipping wall was extended to present dimensions, utilizing high-strength steel and building the current walkway surrounding the pavilion and marina building. So there is a, at present, we use nine by nine, 10 foot long hemlock timbers that are installed on the river pilings, which provide protection from the mooring ships. So this basically buffers the cruise ships, you know, in terms of keeping them away from rubbing directly on the steel. So in the years prior to 2016, the port was used minimally, anywhere from two to eight times a season. And now we're seeing a significant uptick. I believe this year we've had 31 vessels that will be docking at this location. I'll just move forward here. So the dock itself can accommodate vessels up to 560 feet long and a depth of 20 feet. As mentioned, we had 31 ships for this year with an average of 200 passengers. And already for 2023, we have 19 ships that are planning to dock here. And the impact of tourism with these vessels, you know, I think, you know, the major contribution at this time is the associated bus tours, where the passengers that are on the vessels come off, hop on tours and hit our cultural attractions. So, you know, there's a net benefit to the art gallery, to the bush plane, to Ermatinger and the museum. And I'd like to discuss this a little bit further, you know, based on some of the comments that I've heard from Kelly and others about how we activate the waterfront and look at programming for that. Because I think there is a potential for increased benefits to the community. So as mentioned, the offenders themselves take a severe impact from cruise ships. We've got at present 60 wood fenders. We've replaced 10 of them in 2016 for about $10,600. The lifespan with the hemlock fenders is not great. You're looking at anywhere from two to a maximum of, you know, five years, but generally they're failing based on the heavy usage in less than two years. So if these aren't present, then they cause damage to the cruise ships, which obviously none of them went to sea. And we'll see them as a result, start docking more frequently on the Sioux Michigan side. So you can see here the wood's missing. So you've got the hinges sticking directly out with the potential to rub up against those cruise ships. So the proposal is to replace those fenders with these floating fenders, which have a much larger lifespan, upwards of 10 years or more. Believe these are the current fenders that are being used at the Purvis Marina. And in discussions with them, the lifespan has been over 10 years. So there's a great deal of protection there. There's no underwater work that's needed, you know, should they require maintenance or replacement. And they give increased protection for the vessels rather than what you're seeing just with the wood fenders themselves. So we are looking at replacing them. We'd only need 10 of them to replace it.
